headlines.title: U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU
headlines.summary: This is the tape-mover right here — new Section 301 levies hitting China, the EU, and a dozen others simultaneously is a multi-sector gut punch touching everything from semiconductors to autos to consumer goods. When you slap tariffs on that many partners at once, you're not just repricing trade flows, you're repricing global supply chains, and every multinational on the S&P 500 has to recalculate. Watch the long bond and the dollar for the first read on how bad the damage is.

headlines.title: S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk
headlines.summary: S&P putting a notch-cut warning on Nvidia's credit is a fresh body blow to a stock that's already been through the wringer — a ratings action from a major agency signals the governance soap opera isn't just a headline risk, it's now a balance-sheet risk. This widens the blast radius beyond NVDA itself, hitting the whole AI infrastructure trade: AMD, SMCI, the hyperscalers who depend on Nvidia silicon. The bid in NVDA was already fragile; this doesn't help.

headlines.title: Asia's stock markets dive as doubts to swirl over AI boom
headlines.summary: When Seoul drops 3.7% and Taiwan gets hit for nearly 9% at the worst point, that's not noise — that's the AI supply chain repricing in real time, and it sets the tone for the U.S. open. South Korea and Taiwan are ground zero for the chip ecosystem, so moves of that magnitude in those markets are a leading indicator for what NVDA, AMD, and the Nasdaq are going to do when the bell rings. The AI glut fears are doing the heavy lifting here, and they don't resolve in a day.
